Title: 3 Everyday Foods That Feed Vaginal Yeast Infections

Description:
Most women will deal with a vaginal yeast infection at some point. Candida, one of the fungi behind it, thrives on sugar - and sweets, refined carbs like white bread and rice, and beer or sweet wine can all give it more fuel to grow.

None of them need to disappear for good - try nuts or a boiled egg instead of sweets, whole grain instead of white bread, and sparkling water instead of beer or sweet wine.

Watch to find out why.

platforms.title: 3 Everyday Foods That Can Fuel Vaginal Yeast Infections (and What to Eat Instead)
platforms.meta_description: Vaginal yeast infections aren't just about hygiene. Sugar, refined carbs, and alcohol can feed Candida overgrowth, especially when blood sugar runs high.
platforms.body_html:
Most women will deal with a vaginal yeast infection at some point, and it's easy to assume hygiene is the only thing that matters. But according to the CDC, certain everyday habits, including diet, can make it easier for Candida to overgrow, especially when blood sugar runs high. Here are three everyday foods worth a second look, and what tends to work better instead.

Sugar and refined carbs feed the yeast

Candida, the fungus behind most vaginal yeast infections, uses sugar as an energy source. The CDC notes that women with diabetes have a higher risk of yeast infections, in part because high blood sugar can show up in urine and encourage yeast to grow. Sweets like cookies and candy spike blood sugar quickly, and refined carbs like white bread and white rice can do much the same thing.

Alcohol adds a second hit

Beer and sweet wine combine sugar and alcohol in the same glass. Alcohol can also put extra strain on the immune system, making it a bit harder for the body to keep Candida in check on top of the blood sugar swings.

What actually helps

  • Swap sweets for nuts or a boiled egg — satisfies a craving without the same blood sugar spike.
  • Choose whole grain bread over white — whole grains raise blood sugar more slowly than refined carbs.
  • Alternate alcohol with sparkling water — cuts down the total sugar and alcohol in one sitting.
  • Wear breathable, cotton underwear — a small habit that helps keep the area dry rather than warm and damp, conditions yeast tends to prefer.

The bottom line

None of these foods need to disappear completely — moderating them and swapping in the alternatives above can ease the burden over time, especially for anyone managing blood sugar. This article is for general information only and isn't medical advice; frequent or severe symptoms are worth discussing with a doctor.
